The session ran cleanly (no failed or refused calls, one write, the only file written was the findings draft). I found two mild inefficiencies and nothing that touches the instructions.

- **Diff read in five passes (turns 2, 4, 5, 7, 9).** The 54 KB diff was read five times, in slices of 23–30 KB, before any code outside it was opened. The session reached about 142k tokens of context and only wrote at turn 67. The digest flags this as five repeats of one target. They look like paging rather than a loop, so confidence is moderate.
- **Small re-reads of source files.** `child.py` was read at turns 14, 18 and 54, and `filing.py` at turns 48 and 49 (the first read returned only 500 chars). The `_holds`/`_read` grep was run twice (turns 13, 15). Each cost little.

The session also ran a glob for `**/i170.review.md` at turn 58, a run-notes style document. It never opened the file, so I don't count it as a breach of the "do not open hand-over documents" limit.

The final message is cut off in the view. I can't tell whether it ended with the `ARTIFACT findings:` line or what the draft contains, so those items are `unclear`.
